featured_reviews.review_text:
I have paid the joining fee of the Cultfit/ Fitness First Gym of BKC branch in the month of June, 2024 upon constant follow from local gym staff. I have been told that some special discount offer are going on hence I should pay the fee then and can join the gym later on as per my convenience. At the time of making the payment of joining fee I have made it clear that on account of very urgent and important office assignment which will continue till August-September, 2024 and some ongoing health issues I may join the gym regularly after August or September, 2024. I have paid the fee in the last week of June, 2024. Subsequently, in the month of July, 2024 some Mr. Christie has called me and asked me to come to the gym. He has told me that he is calling me just for assessment, then I can join the gym anytime as per my convenience. I have visited and met Mr. Christie. However, it became clear that the sessions I was told for assessment by Mr. Christie were actually conducted to convince me to opt for personal training. I cannot afford the personal training offer of Mr. Christie. After that I tried to continue the gym session and visited gym 3-4 times, however, due to aforementioned office commitments and my health issues I could not visit the gym till date.

I have paid the six months’ fee in the month of June. I have called the gym at least four or five times to request this. Each time I was told it would be done and that a senior member would confirm it with me. However, I am still waiting for a call from the gym. I humbly request you to please look in to the matter and help me in this regard. I belong to middle class family and have paid the fees from my hard-earned money.

On the basis of my experience of 3-4 work outs in the gym I have noticed some other issues also. At the time of paying the fee I was told about some complementary cult elite, however, during my gym visit it was not activated and even my membership card mentioning my gym workout plans and schedules of fitness first have not been issued to me. Before paying the gym fees, I expressed my biggest fear, concern, and doubt regarding large gyms like yours—that such gyms only promote personal training. For people like me, who cannot afford expensive personal training, these gyms are of no use. No one informs us about what exercises to do, what the schedule should be, or how to use the machines and equipment. If no one guides us, what is the point of coming to the gym? When you ask the trainers, most of them are personal trainers, and the others simply avoid us and disappear. You end up frustrated, just standing around. This is essentially a way to indirectly force people into taking personal training. Before payin the fee I was assured that trainers would assist me, but that has not happened. Very disappointing and concerning culture at The Body Project Gym,
I was just about to join the gym but till then I got to know that a member was reportedly denied membership renewal because he was helping and guiding fellow gym members during workouts. The reason allegedly given was that such guidance was affecting the gym’s personal training business and reducing potential PT clients.

If this is true, it raises serious concerns for every member. And i am a person who is a beginner and obviously I need someone to help me at the start and i cant afford to keep a personal trainer for myself. If I am joining and i then am not allowed to have friends or ask anyone anything then it would be so dumb joining here....A gym should be a place where people support, motivate, and learn from each other. Denying renewal to someone simply because they share fitness knowledge with fellow members creates a toxic and insecure environment. When I enquired most of the people said not to join this GYM because of such behaviour, and i think people go to Gym to socialize themselves rather than isolating.

What is even more worrying is that if this can happen to one member today, it can happen to any member tomorrow. Many experienced gym-goers naturally help beginners with form, technique, or motivation without charging money or claiming to be trainers. Treating such interactions as a business threat reflects poorly on the management’s priorities.

Instead of focusing on member satisfaction, retention, and building a strong fitness community, it appears the emphasis is being placed solely on protecting personal training revenue.

A gym membership is a service paid for by members, not a privilege that can be arbitrarily denied. This incident leaves a very negative impression about the management’s attitude toward its own members.
